task: Grade a 1–3 page landscape of the full 220-paper corpus for coverage of recurring methods, major findings, cross-paper patterns and evidence limitations.

nuggets.text: Matched controls repeatedly weaken proposed explanations for performance gains or apparently meaningful mechanistic signals.
Strong aggregate or proxy scores can coexist with poor local behavior, trajectory fidelity, localization or downstream decision value.
Structured compression exploits geometric alignment, low-rank structure and residual redundancy to reduce model or KV-cache costs.
Realized efficiency depends on memory traffic, execution conditions, hardware topology and complete workflow costs.
Frozen backbones support useful adaptation through instruction rewriting, activation transforms, belief updates, routed adapters or trained auxiliary models.
Distillation quality depends on student-compatible supervision; privileged shortcuts, inherited base-policy bias and invalid teacher coordination can obstruct transfer.
Conditioning exploration incentives on correctness or successful behavior improves useful diversity and generalization.
Intermediate or token-level credit and explicit correction of stale trajectories improve the efficiency of RL post-training.
Additional computation or updates have context-dependent value; frequent re-solving and unconditional refinement can worsen outcomes.
Forecasting, sampling and asynchronous learning require treatment of accumulated, path-dependent errors beyond isolated one-step accuracy.
Physical equations, conservation laws, boundary conditions and symmetries are repeatedly embedded in scientific models to improve validity or extrapolation.
Transfer and adaptation benefits depend on the target task, representation and distribution shift; stronger source modeling or additional adaptation can hurt target performance.
Flow and diffusion models recur as frameworks for probabilistic forecasting, spatial-field generation, multimodal generation and inverse-problem inference.
Covariance structure and coordinated latent randomness materially affect joint predictive likelihood and generation coherence.
Uncertainty and safety assessment must match the deployment distribution and the relevant outcome region, selected subset or risk tail.
Identifiability and guaranteed decisions can fail when retained state or observations cannot distinguish alternatives relevant to the requested operation.
Online-learning guarantees explicitly tie achievable rates to noise moments, distribution-change assumptions and available feedback.
Compact models and simpler baselines can outperform more elaborate comparators in small-data learning, forecasting and anomaly detection.
Weak, self-supervised and unpaired methods reduce dependence on dense labels or paired observations for learning useful representations.
Agentic search has produced useful scientific models, valid kernels, mathematical constructions and executable control programs under task-specific evaluation.
Robot-agent reliability remains limited by instruction sensitivity and inaccurate or hallucinated task state.
Behavioral interventions need explicit preservation of benign or successful capabilities because broad benchmark stability can hide collateral damage.
Spectral rank is not a universal health or robustness score; its interpretation depends on architecture, training conditions and the representation measured.
Feedback through agent interaction or recursive synthetic-data training can reinforce bias and reduce behavioral diversity.

integration_facts.text: Across distillation, contextual inputs, graph transfer and domain adaptation, stronger source performance or additional information can hurt when the transferred signal is incompatible with the downstream learner or task.

A recurring efficiency strategy moves expensive learning or search offline and reuses its results through graph-free students, compact decoders, adapters, stored experience or executable programs and priors.

Safety, forecasting, anomaly detection and verification share a mismatch between aggregate success and operational reliability: local benign behavior, complete trajectories, localization and failures conditional on acceptance require separate evaluation.

Stateful systems require reasoning over whole trajectories: forecast initialization errors, numerical amplification, stale-policy errors and update schedules depend on accumulated state and future consequences.

Equations and symmetry improve several scientific surrogates, yet forward-model fidelity and physical consistency do not ensure accurate inverse estimates or forecasts; structural priors must suit the intended prediction problem.

Unlearning, sensing, latent recovery and safety share an information-sufficiency boundary: guarantees require observations or retained state that distinguish the alternatives relevant to the requested operation.

Method rankings are conditional on data regime, evaluation target and resource model: compact models can win on constrained data, larger models benefit from diverse pretraining, and hardware or interaction costs can reverse apparent efficiency advantages.

Diversity depends on the feedback mechanism: rewarding successful exploration helps, while interacting agents or self-consuming training can homogenize behavior. Reference-data injection stabilizes some analyzed synthetic-training dynamics, but these studies do not establish a universal remedy.

answer_key.q: What is the corpus's central evaluation lesson?
answer_key.a: Progress requires matched controls, strong baselines and deployment-relevant tests. Aggregate accuracy, likelihood or proxy improvements can conceal local regressions, conditional risk, poor trajectories or absent decision value.

answer_key.q: What recurring strategies reduce model and inference costs?
answer_key.a: Structured compression and quantization, sparse retrieval, state reuse, frozen-backbone adaptation and offline distillation or program generation. Their value depends on retained capabilities and actual memory, latency, hardware and workflow costs.

answer_key.q: What makes RL post-training and teacher transfer more effective?
answer_key.a: Student-compatible supervision, successful or quality-filtered diversity, useful intermediate credit, stale-trajectory correction and appropriate compute allocation. Better teachers, richer inputs and additional updates are not automatically beneficial.

answer_key.q: What unifies advances in scientific machine learning, and what limits their scope?
answer_key.a: Physics-aware structure, probabilistic flow/diffusion models and cross-domain training improve scientific surrogates. Claims still require validation on long rollouts, inverse tasks, new geometries and relevant distribution shifts, including independently varied climate forcings.

answer_key.q: What common boundary appears in the theoretical results?
answer_key.a: Recoverability and achievable rates depend on available information and explicit noise, feedback and dynamics assumptions. Missing distinguishing information can make deletion, latent recovery or timely safe action impossible.

answer_key.q: What does the corpus establish about autonomous agents and behavioral safety?
answer_key.a: Agents achieve useful task-specific discoveries and executable improvements, while grounding, state tracking and sustained execution remain fragile. Behavioral repairs require capability-retention checks and evaluation of local, conditional and tail risks.
